long_biography.plain_text:
Trained in civil aviation, Kozeruk entered aircraft maintenance before establishing BVT with partners. The business began in passenger and cargo transport, then added food imports for northern Russian markets. After managing BVT, he spent a decade advising Gazprom Invest Yug on investment projects.

Property development became his next professional chapter. Kozeruk served on MR Group's board and led GVSU Center, a general contractor, before joining Granel as a co-investor in a residential project. His visible pattern combines advisory experience, company stakes and project participation while other executives carry operating responsibility. The scale and origin of his personal fortune remain undisclosed.

uncertainties: Identity is high-confidence but not conclusive. The uncommon full patronymic name and career converge across established reporting and registry-derived records, but transliteration varies among Anatoly, Anatoliy, Nikolaevich and Nikolayevich.

Search results contain several conflicting biographies for people with the identical Cyrillic full name, including different birth dates and occupations. None of that namesake material was used for accepted claims.

The input's 10 June 1966 birth date appears in some public lists and profiles, but no sufficiently authoritative reviewed source independently verified it. Existing birth fields were preserved without using them to expand the biography.

Several low-quality biography pages name Saint Petersburg or Leningrad as Kozeruk's birthplace. Because these pages appear search-engine-optimised and conflict with namesake content, place of birth remains blank.

Kommersant's 2017 and 2018 Kozeruk interviews are explicitly labelled sponsored. They are used only for self-described chronology already corroborated in material part by later independent reporting, not for wealth or ownership claims.

RBC Companies, За честный бизнес and B2B.house reproduce public registry data rather than constituting first-party company biographies. Their matching full name and tax identifier support registered legal interests, but not undisclosed beneficial ownership beyond those entries.

The 99.9 percent Center Project and 100 percent Khodynsky Park figures describe registered participation in nominal capital. They do not establish the market value of either company or the size of Kozeruk's personal fortune.

Real Estate is the best-supported current primary industry because recent activity and registered interests cluster in Moscow development and property management. The public record does not establish the relative value of all holdings.

Real Estate is assigned as the wealth-creation industry because Forbes documents substantial personal property acquisitions, BVT's investment in a Moscow business centre and Kozeruk's partnerships on further developments, with later sources confirming continued residential investment. The score is capped because the contribution of the earlier transport and trading business is not quantified.

Broad Self-made is inferred from Kozeruk's documented co-founding of BVT and the later sequence of personally attributed property investments and controlling project-company interests. Independent start and advantaged start remain unassigned because launch capital and family context are not public; no positive evidence supports inheritance or family transfer.

Investor is the best-supported current relationship based on a directly reported co-investment and several registered project-company interests; it does not imply ownership of every company where Kozeruk held an advisory, board or executive role.

Politics, sanctions, allegations, legal matters and controversies were excluded by scope and do not appear in the dossier's accepted evidence or biographies.

Under the amended reasonable-inference policy, the previously Unknown HNWI fields are resolved as Real Estate and broad Self-made. The broad origin label does not assert an independent start: launch capital, family context and acquisition financing remain undisclosed. The dossier does not infer beneficial ownership of former employers. Conflicting namesake material and all excluded topics remain outside the accepted evidence.
